newsitem.title: UK: IGC raises world 1997 coarse grains output estimate.
newsitem.headline: IGC raises world 1997 coarse grains output estimate.

text.p: The International Grains Council (IGC) on Thursday raised its estimate for 1997 world coarse grains output by six million tonnes to a record 903 million, after 892 million in 1996.
The increase was mainly due to higher crop expectations in the U.S. -- particularly maize -- , where the overall estimate jumped by six million tonnes to 277.1 million.
U.S. coarse grains output reached 267.6 million in 1996, the IGC said.

The forecast for coarse grains stocks was also sharply higher at 121 million tonnes -- the highest since 1993 -- after the IGC's previous forecast of 116 million. 1996 stocks were estimated at 113 million tonnes.

Lower expectations for Russia accounted for most of the reduced forecast for CIS 1997 output in general, cut by 2.2 million tonnes to 59.7 million. Russia was expected to turn out 33.5 million tonnes, down on the previous forecast of 35.2 million and just below the 1996 result of 33.0 million.

World coarse grains consumption was pegged one million tonnes higher at a record 896 million tonnes for 1997/98, with increases in most geographical areas. This compared with 869 million tonnes in 1996/97, the IGC said.
